The image now carries this repo's version, so every update Unraid offers has its own number. Four upstream components move forward with it.

## ✨ Added

- **Synapse [v1.162.0](https://github.com/element-hq/synapse/releases/tag/v1.162.0).**
- **Matrix Authentication Service [1.26.0](https://github.com/element-hq/matrix-authentication-service/releases/tag/v1.26.0).** Only reached when Delegated Auth is switched on; the default path is untouched.
- **Element Web [v1.12.30](https://github.com/element-hq/element-web/releases/tag/v1.12.30).**
- **Ketesa [v1.5.1](https://github.com/etkecc/ketesa/releases/tag/v1.5.1).**

## ⚡ Improved

- **Image tags follow the repo version.** A release `vX.Y.Z` is published as `X.Y.Z`, `X.Y`, `X` and `latest`, and `latest` moves only with a release. Tags and the version label used to come from the newest Synapse release, so a rebuild without a new Synapse showed up in Unraid as the same update again. The Synapse version inside is in the image label `io.github.junkerderprovinz.matrix.synapse-version`.
- **A merge to main builds `edge`, and only when the image changes.** New Synapse releases arrive through Renovate and ship with the next release instead of an hourly check. Commits that leave the image alone, such as docs or the forum thread, no longer trigger a build.
- **Synapse-version tags are no longer published.** A template pinned to a tag like `1.161.0` keeps that image; switch it to `latest` or to a release such as `3.4.0` to keep getting updates.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **gosu comes from the static upstream build.** Debian's package was built with Go 1.24.4 and carried two standard-library vulnerabilities the binary could actually reach (GO-2026-4602 and GO-2025-3956). The static `tianon/gosu` 1.19 build has neither.

## 🎨 Design

- **A shorter README with new pictures.** It opens with download buttons, shows Element Web and the Ketesa admin page on two new screenshots, and keeps the setup to what a first start needs.
